extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, affected applicants/obligors, policy stakeholders, and commenters on the DHS proposed public charge rule
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards in the DHS proposed public-charge rule governing Requests for Evidence (RFEs), the newly-proposed public charge bond process (forms, fees, acceptance, breach and cancellation rules), cost/time-burden estimation methods, and related impact/estimation methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS discretion to issue RFE for Form I-944
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all nonimmigrants who apply for extension of stay or change of status would be required to file Form I-944; USCIS officers would be able to exercise discretion regarding whether it would be necessary to issue a RFE for the submission of Form I-944.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudication officers may issue an RFE when, in their judgment, additional financial/health/education detail is necessary to determine whether an individual has received, is receiving, or is likely to receive public benefits. DHS is unable to estimate how many RFEs officers will issue because issuance is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs/time burden associated with filing Form I-944
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the costs for filing Form I-944 include the opportunity cost of time (4.5 hours) and the cost to obtain a credit report and credit score ($19.95 per beneficiary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS uses an average total rate of compensation of $35.78 per hour to calculate an opportunity cost of $161.01 per beneficiary (4.5 hrs * $35.78). For population-level costs multiply per-applicant cost by estimated annual filings (e.g., Form I-129: 336,335; Form I-129CW: 6,307; Form I-539: 174,866). DHS assumes beneficiary, not petitioner, completes Form I-944 when a petitioner receives an RFE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for calculating opportunity cost of time for form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS calculates per-applicant opportunity cost of time by multiplying an average total rate of compensation (e.g., $35.78/hour or minimum wage $10.66/hour as specified) by the estimated hours to complete the form, then multiplies by estimated annual population filing the form to get annual total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/formulas provided in preamble (e.g., I-539 current: $35.78/hr * 1.88 hrs = $67.27; proposed: $35.78/hr * 2.38 hrs = $85.16). DHS rounds intermediate and final results and reports totals and differences (new costs = proposed annual cost – current annual cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of public charge bond process and acceptable bond forms
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to amend regulations to establish a bond process for adjustment applicants deemed likely to become a public charge. A public charge bond may be secured by cash or cash equivalents (cashier's checks or money orders) in the full amount of the bond, or underwritten by a surety company certified by the Department of the Treasury under 31 U.S.C. 9304-9308.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS plans initially to allow surety bonds only. DHS approval of the bond will consider whether the alien has received public benefits as defined in the proposed rule or breached any bond conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for bond approval and what constitutes a breach
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS approval of a public charge bond and determination of breach would be based on whether the alien has received public benefits as defined in the proposed rule or whether the alien has breached any other condition imposed as part of the public charge bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an alien receives public benefits after adjustment of status (as defined in proposed 8 CFR 212.21(b)), DHS would declare the bond breached. Bonds may also be breached for failure to comply with bond-imposed conditions (see proposed 8 CFR 213.1(h)). Upon breach DHS notifies obligor and informs of appeal options to AAO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary issuance and amount determination of public charge bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: Public charge bonds would be issued at the Secretary's discretion when an alien seeking adjustment is found inadmissible based on public charge grounds; the amount would be determined at the discretion of the adjudication officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed minimum bond amount is $10,000 annually (adjusted for inflation and rounded up to the nearest dollar), but the adjudication officer otherwise sets the bond amount. DHS will notify the alien if permitted to post a bond and of the acceptable bond type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms required for bond posting, cancellation, and related actions
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual/entity would submit a public charge bond using new Public Charge Bond form (Form I-945). DHS proposes to use Form I-356 for Request for Cancellation of Public Charge Bond. Form I-407 must be completed when an alien or obligor/co-obligor seeks to cancel the public charge bond on account of the alien's permanent departure from the United States. Notice of Appeal or Motion (Form I-290B) is used to appeal certain decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble explains which forms are used in which situations (posting, cancellation, appeal, abandonment). Use of I-407 also informs alien of the right to a hearing before an immigration judge regarding abandonment of LPR status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and procedures for cancellation of public charge bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: A public charge bond must be canceled when an alien with a bond dies, departs the United States permanently, or is naturalized or otherwise obtains U.S. citizenship, provided the individual has not received public benefits (as defined) prior to death, departure, or naturalization and a request for cancellation has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS must also cancel the bond following the fifth anniversary of admission of the LPR if a request for cancellation is filed and the alien has not received any public benefits after adjustment. The bond must be canceled if the alien obtains an immigration status exempt from public charge inadmissibility after initial grant, provided a cancellation request is filed and the bond conditions were not breached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution of bonds and substitution filing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A public charge bond may be cancelled by DHS after a suitable substitute has been submitted for an unlimited bond or a bond of limited duration that bears an expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For substitution of another bond, no request to cancel must be filed to allow substitution, as outlined in proposed 8 CFR 213.1(f). Because USCIS does not examine whether the bond could be breached for substitution, substitution need not be accompanied by filing of Form I-356 in that situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that surety companies be Treasury-certified
rubrics_metrics.description: If DHS accepts a surety bond, it would accept only a bond underwritten by surety companies certified by the Department of the Treasury, as outlined in proposed 8 CFR 103.6(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to 31 U.S.C. 9304-9308 and Treasury Bureau of the Fiscal Service resources; USCIS plans to initially allow surety bonds only (see ICE proposed procedures referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost structure for securing surety bonds (premium percentage)
rubrics_metrics.description: When posting a surety bond, an individual generally pays between 1 percent to 15 percent of the bond amount for a surety company to post a bond. The percentage may depend on the individual's credit score where those with higher credit scores would be required to pay a lower percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS cites industry source examples (suretybondauthority.com) for illustrative premium ranges and notes that obligors will also pay the filing fee and opportunity cost of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fees, time burdens, and per-applicant cost estimates for bond-related forms
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes fees and estimates time burdens for bond-related forms: Form I-945 filing fee $25.00; time burden 60 minutes (1.0 hour) per obligor; opportunity cost using minimum wage $10.66/hr gives $10.66 per applicant. Form I-356 filing fee $25.00; time burden 45 minutes (0.75 hr); opportunity cost $8.00. Form I-290B fee $675; time burden 1.5 hrs; opportunity cost $15.99; estimated postage $3.75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS aggregates per-applicant costs (e.g., minimum cost per obligor to file I-945 = $25.00 fee + $10.66 time = $35.66, plus surety premiums). DHS uses estimated annual populations to project totals (e.g., ~960 aliens eligible to file I-945 -> ~$34,234 annual minimum). Fee for I-290B may be waived with Form I-912 if inability to pay; DHS reports total per-applicant cost of $693.74 for I-290B excluding bond costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: DHS inability to precisely estimate RFE issuance rates; presentation of cost ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS is unable to estimate the actual number of RFEs adjudication officers may issue to require Form I-944 because such RFEs would be issued on a discretionary basis; DHS presents a range of RFEs that could be issued and associated annual costs at various percentage issuance rates (100%, 90%, 75%, 50%, 25%, 10%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 48 presents estimated annual costs associated with submission of Form I-944 based on the percentage of the total population issued an RFE for each form type (I-129, I-129CW, I-539). Use population estimates and per-applicant costs to compute scenario totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge determination: weighting of past or current receipt of public benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposed rule, DHS would consider past or current receipt of public benefits, defined in 212.21(b), as identified a heavily weighed factor for purposes of public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble lists and describes public benefits programs considered. Receipt (past or current) of certain public benefits identified in the proposed rule may lead to a finding that an individual is likely to become a public charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact assessment: reductions in transfer payments and indirect impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates not only direct costs of the proposed rule but also reductions in transfer payments from federal and state government to certain individuals who receive public benefits, and discusses indirect impacts borne by entities not directly regulated (e.g., hospital systems, state agencies) due to changes in behavior caused by the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect costs include familiarization with the rule for entities that want to understand changes in federal/state transfer payments. DHS qualitatively acknowledges the potential admission-denial impact for aliens outside the U.S. and inability to quantify some of these effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population-estimation methodology for affected households and recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS uses the American Community Survey (ACS) and beneficiary data from each benefits program to estimate the population of public benefits recipients who are members of households that include foreign-born non-citizens, using the ACS estimated average household size for foreign-born households (3.35 persons) and other ACS tabulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS describes calculations (e.g., percent foreign-born non-citizen households = 6.97%) and multiplication by average household size to estimate number of recipients. Sources and caution about data differences (e.g., SIPP versus ACS) are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and motion procedures following bond breach or cancellation denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon learning of a breach of a public charge bond, DHS would notify the obligor that the bond has been declared breached and inform the obligor of the possibility to appeal the determination to the USCIS Administrative Appeals Office (AAO). Notice of Appeal or Motion (Form I-290B) is used to file an appeal or motion to reopen or reconsider certain decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing fee for Form I-290B is $675 per obligor; fee may be waived with Form I-912 if inability to pay. Time burden and postage estimates are provided; DHS explains where appeal fits in the statutory/regulatory process (see proposed 8 CFR 213.1(g) and 8 CFR 103.7(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No new costs imposed on Form I-407 filers for bond cancellation upon departure
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule requires an alien must complete and submit Form I-407 when seeking to cancel the public charge bond upon permanent departure from the United States. However, this proposed rule would not impose additional new costs to Form I-407 filers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form I-407 is used by lawful permanent residents outside the U.S. or at a Port of Entry who want to abandon LPR status and informs them of the right to an IJ hearing to determine whether status was lost due to abandonment.
